summary: This script fetches 10 random users from an online API, extracts relevant information like their name and email, and formats everything into a Markdown table that gets printed to the screen. It's a simple data-fetching and formatting pipeline.

explanations.7: This imports type hints so we can declare what kinds of data our functions expect and return—like saying 'this function returns a list of dictionaries' rather than just 'a list'.
explanations.15: We're creating a dictionary with the query parameters to send to the API—in this case, asking for 10 results instead of the default.
explanations.17: We're making an HTTP GET request to the API URL with those parameters, and storing the response object so we can check if it succeeded and extract the data.
explanations.22: This checks if the HTTP request failed (like a 404 or 500 error) and raises an exception if it did, so we don't accidentally try to process bad data.
explanations.24: We're converting the response from the API (which is formatted as JSON text) into a Python dictionary so we can access the data using keys.
explanations.34: This creates the separator row in Markdown tables—the dashes under the headers that tell Markdown to treat the first row as column titles.
explanations.37: We're combining the user's first and last name into a single string using an f-string, which lets us embed variables directly into text.
